title: Reconcile unpinned lockfiles across Python/JS/Go and retire legacy compatibility surface
creator: Jonas Rivera
description: We have drift across client SDKs where some ecosystems use loose or partially-pinned dependency ranges, multiple lockfile formats, and compatibility shims that keep legacy API surface alive. This ticket consolidates dependency pinning strategy, normalizes lockfile maintenance across Python/JS/Go, upgrades critical transitive dependencies (http libraries, protobufs, auth libs), and removes the runtime compatibility surface that was introduced for historical clients. Goal: reduce dependency churn, shrink install footprints, improve cold-start latency in serverless environments, and make future security upgrades predictable.
background: Over the last two years we introduced compatibility wrappers and soft constraints to ease cross-language parity while onboarding model tooling and new runtime features. Consequences: duplicated transitive dependency versions, CI flakiness from inconsistent lockfiles, larger docker images for lightweight Lambda-style clients, and a handful of low-severity CVEs that required multiple partial fixes. Security tooling (Dependabot/Snyk) shows a growing set of alerts that are hard to remediate because lockfile strategies differ between repos.
technical_approach: 1) Audit current dependency manifests and lockfiles across repos: client-python, client-js, client-go. 2) Propose a canonical pinning policy: pinned runtime deps in lockfiles, caret ranges for dev deps only. 3) Adopt a single lockfile strategy per language (pip-tools + constraints for Python, npm ci with package-lock.json for Node, go.mod tidy + go.sum hygiene for Go). 4) Upgrade prioritized libs to safe, tested versions (requests/httpx -> 3.x where available; axios -> 1.4+; go-http clients consistent at v1.x). 5) Replace compatibility shims in client surface with opt-in adapters documented in migration notes. 6) Run benchmarks and CI matrix including older OS images and serverless cold start profiles. 7) Roll out in canary with step-down fallback via feature flag if any production regressions appear.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three SDK repos have updated manifests and committed lockfiles following the new pinning policy.
- No transitive CVEs with high severity remain unmitigated (low/medium allowed with documented mitigation).
- Integration tests (full matrix) pass in CI for node 16/18/20, python 3.9/3.10/3.11, and Go 1.20/1.21.
- Measured cold-start memory and latency improved or unchanged for our sample serverless benchmark (target: <= +1% latency, preferably -5%); image size reduced for python wheel by >= 8%.
- Public SDK changelogs and migration guide published with clear removal of deprecated compatibility surface and API examples for migrated code paths.

risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Tightening pins may lead to initial breakages for customers but reduces long-term bit-rot; mitigations: coordinated changelog and opt-in adapters.
- Upgrading to newer http client major versions can change behavior (timeouts, redirects); we will run conformance tests against our integration suite.
- Removing shims simplifies surface but forces some customers to change import paths; provide migration helpers and 3-month compatibility branch as an emergency fallback.
measured_outcomes: Early branch benchmarks: python wheel size reduced by 12% when removing legacy shim code and consolidating requests->httpx usage. Serverless cold-start median latency improved by 6% in our benchmark (python 3.10 on AWS Lambda warm/cold traces). CI runtime decreased by ~10% after lockfile dedupe and pruning of dev-only install steps.
